meta.task: Build our weekly engineering digest — pull the week's posts from our feeds, pick the ten that matter, summarize them, and send the issue
meta.title: Automate a Weekly Newsletter Digest
meta.promptIntro: Build our weekly engineering digest: pull the week's posts from our feeds, pick the ten that matter, summarize them, and send the issue. Set the gathering and summarizing up to run unattended, keep the editor's pick and a rendering check in the loop, and leave the whole thing repeating next week without being rebuilt.

nodes.label: Collect the feeds and the house rules
nodes.description: Gather the source list, the audience, the send day, the tone, and what actually counts as worth including.

nodes.label: Write a fetcher per source
nodes.description: Hand-write the HTTP calls and feed parsing for every source: RSS here, Atom there, and screen-scraping for the sites with no feed at all.

nodes.label: Wrap every call in retries and timeouts
nodes.description: Add the retry logic, the timeouts, and the backoff that keep one slow source from hanging the whole run.

nodes.label: Re-fix the parsers that broke this week
nodes.description: Find which sources changed their markup since last run and patch each parser before the gathering can even start.

nodes.label: Dedupe and normalize the items
nodes.description: The same story arrives from five sources with five titles: strip tracking parameters, match the duplicates, fill in missing authors and dates, and cut to the last seven days.

nodes.label: Rank what actually matters this week
nodes.description: Judge each item against the house rules and sort the week down to a shortlist worth an editor's time.

nodes.label: Summarize the shortlist, call by call
nodes.description: Open each link, read it, and write the two or three sentences that go in the issue — a hundred model calls a week against a single provider.

nodes.label: Babysit rate limits mid-run
nodes.description: Watch the run for the rate limits and provider errors that land halfway through, and note where the batch stopped so the gaps can be rerun.

nodes.label: Every summary came back?
nodes.description: Did the run finish, or did rate limits and provider errors leave holes in the middle of it?

nodes.label: Editor picks the final ten
nodes.description: A person reads the shortlist and decides what actually ships — the part nobody wants automated.

nodes.label: Assemble the issue
nodes.description: Pour the picks into the HTML and plain-text templates, escape what needs escaping, and check every link resolves.

nodes.label: Send a test to yourself
nodes.description: Send the draft to your own inbox and open it in the mail clients your readers actually use.

nodes.label: Renders everywhere?
nodes.description: Does it hold together in the clients that matter, or has one of them eaten the layout again?

nodes.label: Send the issue
nodes.description: Send to the list and watch the first bounces come back.

nodes.label: Wire it to run every week
nodes.description: Put the run on a schedule, store the credentials somewhere it can reach, and make failures shout instead of skipping a week quietly.

nodes.label: Digest shipped and scheduled
nodes.description: This week's issue is out, and the run repeats on its own next week.

suggestions.name: modelcontextprotocol/servers
suggestions.claim: Official gallery of reference MCP servers — copy-paste connector starting points.
suggestions.promptFragment: Start the gathering step from modelcontextprotocol/servers rather than writing the fetching plumbing yourself: take the reference server closest to pulling web content and adapt it to the source list. Wire that up before anything is ranked, so every source arrives through one connector instead of a pile of one-off HTTP calls and hand-tuned retries.

replaceWith.label: Adapt a reference fetch server
replaceWith.description: One reference MCP server does the fetching for every source — the HTTP, retry, and timeout plumbing comes with it instead of being written by hand.

suggestions.name: diegosouzapw/OmniRoute
suggestions.claim: One endpoint for 290+ AI providers with fallbacks and up to 95% token-cost cuts.
suggestions.promptFragment: Put the summarizing pass behind diegosouzapw/OmniRoute instead of calling one provider directly and rerunning the batch every time it rate-limits: one endpoint, with its routing and quota fallbacks carrying the run through a provider that stalls. Point the summarizer at it before the first weekly run, so a hundred calls finish unattended rather than being nursed.

replaceWith.label: Summarize through one routed endpoint
replaceWith.description: Every summary goes through a single gateway whose quota fallbacks absorb the rate limits that used to halve the batch — no babysitting, nothing to check on afterwards.
